name: a-five-tap-filter-whose-half-width-is-an-integer-absolute-value
rationale: HorizontalFilter reads its tap count from a buffer, halves it, and takes llvm.abs.i32 of that half as the loop bound while starting the loop at its negation -- the only reader of that intrinsic any case reaches, and the value that decides how many taps run and where they start. Five taps with powers-of-ten coefficients make every tap's contribution separable in the result, and the input texel values are distinct per column, so a tap taken at the wrong offset or a loop that runs the wrong number of times changes the output digit by digit rather than by rounding. The sample coordinates land exactly on texel centres at every tap, so no filtering is involved; the two columns at each edge read outside the texture, which pins the address mode of the module's constexpr sampler word: of clamp-to-edge, repeat, mirrored-repeat and clamp-to-zero, only mirrored-repeat reproduces Metal's output. The loop is bounded by the authored tap count of five.

name: linked-zero-destination-random
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: One sample per thread and zero destination width, height, channels, and batch make the sole invocation fail the destination-product bounds check. The six loop-free linked seed reads are exact constants, and no postfix destination callback executes, leaving the bounded poisoned output unchanged. Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: uniform-eight-columns-two-threads-row-end-scalar-path
rationale: Reaching variant of this entry's zero-destination case (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero extents skip every write. Here the random params (binding 29) select the uniform distribution on [0.5, 2.5) with counter step 5 per thread, a single 8-column row (height, channels and batch 1; each magic divisor is (8, 0, 4), exact for indices below 16), and kMPSUserConstant = 0x20 gives kNumSamples = 4 floats. 2 threads, one threadgroup. The six seed words read through prefixPrimary_i are 1 (retained module), so thread t's counter starts at (1 + 5 t, 1, 1, 1) with key (1, 1) and advances by 5 * 2 per step. Thread 0 owns columns 0 to 3, which fit strictly inside the row, so its vector goes to the no-op postfixPrimary_4xf and those columns keep the fill; thread 1 owns columns 4 to 7, where x + 4 = 8 is not below the width, so the chunk loop writes its four values one by one through postfixPrimary_f with counter (6, 1, 1, 1). Each value is Philox4x32-10 (multipliers 0xD2511F53 and 0xCD9E8D57, key steps 0x9E3779B9 and 0xBB67AE85, as in the AIR) mapped as (word & 0x7fffff | 0x3f800000) - 1, times 2.0, plus 0.5: integer work is exact and the float steps are exact (23-bit fractions, a power-of-two scale, an offset of 0.5). Expected columns: ['fill', 'fill', 'fill', 'fill', 1.4269640445709229, 1.183030605316162, 1.0317819118499756, 0.536766767501831]. Each observed column is written at most once, by one thread. The row extent bounds the chunk loop and the remainder; the distribution loop runs once (four samples per Philox call).

name: uniform-eleven-columns-two-threads-remainder-three
rationale: Reaching variant of this entry's zero-destination case (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero extents skip every write. Here the random params (binding 29) select the uniform distribution on [0.5, 2.5) with counter step 5 per thread, a single 11-column row (height, channels and batch 1; each magic divisor is (11, 0, 4), exact for indices below 16), and kMPSUserConstant = 0x20 gives kNumSamples = 4 floats. 2 threads, one threadgroup. The six seed words read through prefixPrimary_i are 1 (retained module), so thread t's counter starts at (1 + 5 t, 1, 1, 1) with key (1, 1) and advances by 5 * 2 per step. One grid-stride chunk covers columns 0 to 7 through the vector path (no-op link, fill kept); the remainder step gives thread 0 columns 8 to 10, three values short of a vector, written one by one through postfixPrimary_f from counter (11, 1, 1, 1); thread 1 has no remainder and column 11 keeps the fill. Each value is Philox4x32-10 (multipliers 0xD2511F53 and 0xCD9E8D57, key steps 0x9E3779B9 and 0xBB67AE85, as in the AIR) mapped as (word & 0x7fffff | 0x3f800000) - 1, times 2.0, plus 0.5: integer work is exact and the float steps are exact (23-bit fractions, a power-of-two scale, an offset of 0.5). Expected columns: ['fill', 'fill', 'fill', 'fill', 'fill', 'fill', 'fill', 'fill', 2.2830958366394043, 1.1715688705444336, 2.0574705600738525, 'fill']. Each observed column is written at most once, by one thread. The row extent bounds the chunk loop and the remainder; the distribution loop runs once (four samples per Philox call).

name: scatter-three-hough-votes-into-distinct-clamped-bins
rationale: Four threads each scale a half texel by 255, round it and read the result as three unsigned bin coordinates. The all-zero texel has a zero vote count and takes the early return, so its bin stays at its seeded value; the other three land on distinct cells of the four-by-three histogram, which makes the atomic adds order-independent and the result exact. One column index and one row index are deliberately past the end so both min clamps are exercised, and the twelve counters are seeded 100..111 so every cell says which vote reached it.

name: load-through-an-aliased-pointer-merge
rationale: A pointer merged from two DISTINCT device buffers and then aliased by the identity pointer cast the frontend spells `bitcast ptr %sel to ptr`, with the index applied to the alias. The merge has no SPIR-V pointer id of its own -- Logical addressing cannot select between two descriptors -- so the alias must carry it; before 29fdc3ef this exact program failed to translate with `native emitter: unknown SSA value`. Measured: 0 of 14,579 corpus sources and 0 of the 1,090 cased sources plus 136 public fixtures reach the alias-carries-a-merge arm, so this case is the only input that does. The condition is per-lane, so both arms are read in one dispatch.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-four-simd-primary

name: decode-an-extended-range-bgr10a8-pair-across-its-signed-bias
rationale: Two ushort textures carry the BGR10 plane and the A8 plane. The colour plane is biased by -384 in i16 and widened SIGNED, so a texel below the bias has to come out negative: 129 becomes -255 and scales to -0.5, where an unsigned widening would read 65281 and land on 128. The alpha plane goes through air.convert.f.f16.u.i16, which is what this case is for. All three colour texels are chosen so the f32 product lands within half a half-ULP of 1.0, 0.5 and -0.5, so the f32 to f16 narrowing absorbs the reciprocal's rounding and the answer is byte-stable. The BGR to RGB swizzle is pinned because the three channels carry three different values.

name: simdgroup-matrix-8x8-through-threadgroup-memory
rationale: `simdgroup_load`/`simdgroup_store` against THREADGROUP memory (`air.simdgroup_matrix_8x8_{load,store}.v64f32.p3f32` and `.v64f16.p3f16`), which no authored case reached: the only corpus host for them is function-constant gated and never translates. The pointer operand is the `[128 x float]` array symbol itself, not an element pointer, so the element address is an `OpAccessChain` INTO the array and not an `OpPtrAccessChain` stride over it. The staging arrays are 128 wide and the leading dimension is 16, so a lowering that assumed an 8-wide stride reads and writes the wrong 64 cells; the 64 slots the 16-stride store never touches stay zero and say so.

name: lut-gemv-xreduce-zero-shape

name: plain-row-sums-public-prefix-matrix-four-rows-eleven-wide
rationale: Reaching variant of this entry's zero-destination case (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero destination extent returns at the bounds check and whose retained prefix callbacks return constants. Constant 115 = 0 and kMPSUserConstant = 0x18000e4 (xMap 0, yMap 1, zMap 2, wMap 3, destination and reduction bounds checks) give the plain path: no LUT and no quantization on either side, nRes 1, nSteps 1; kMPSDeviceCaps = 0 reduces through threadgroup memory instead of SIMD shuffles; constant 122 = 0x010101 gives the table three arrays. The params (binding 29) give dstSize 4, 1, 1, 1 and reductionSize 11. prefixSecondary_f and prefixTertiary_f link the public module validation/fixtures/public/linked/mps_prefix_secondary_tertiary_f_from_buffers (owned MSL, DESIGN D431 item 2), which returns element c.x + 4 (c.y + 4 (c.z + 4 c.w)) of the table's array 1 or 2; the matrix is read through prefixSecondary_f at (r, k), element r + 4k of array 1. The vector operand comes through prefixPrimary_f, which has no public module: its retained module returns 1.0, so each output is a plain row sum. 4 threadgroups of 4 threads: threadgroup r owns row r, thread t takes k = t, t + 4, t + 8 below 11, and the partial sums meet in threadgroup memory; the retained postfixPrimary_f writes the row sum to element r of array 1. Array 1 starts as nonzero integers in [-6, 7] ([-4.0, 3.0, -3.0, 4.0, -2.0, 5.0, -1.0, 6.0] for elements 0 to 7); the observed words are elements 0 to 7 of array 1: the row sums [8.0, 7.0, 6.0, -2.0], then elements 4 to 7 unchanged. Threadgroup r reads only elements congruent to r mod 4 and writes element r, so no threadgroup reads another's output, and its own read of element r precedes the barrier before its write. Integer terms with sums below 2^6 are exact in any order and none is zero. The loops are bounded by reductionSize 11.

name: corner-maxima-of-4x4-blocks-land-as-short-slices-at-the-grid-position
rationale: The census's rwppCornerDetectFirstPass4x4Short writes its explicit imageblock of short4 cells to a texture2d<short> through a slice of [[threads_per_threadgroup]] cells, a runtime extent, at the threadgroup's first grid position; no authored case reached it. Each thread gathers nine 2x2 footprints of the red channel of an RGBA16Sint response texture (the other channels hold 7777, -7777 and 1234, which a gather of another component would read; a pixel-coordinate, clamp-to-edge constexpr sampler at ROI + 4 gid, offsets 0, 2, 4 on each axis), walks a 4x4 block's candidates with strict signed comparisons against the maxima of their neighbours, and stores (x, y, response, 0) of the block's surviving maximum, or zeros. The response is a seeded field of small integers (-40 to 40) so that ties are common and the strict comparisons decide; everything is integer, so the answer is exact. The ROI (4, 4) and an 8x8 grid of 4x4 threadgroups keep every gathered texel inside the 64x64 texture (3 to 36). The 8x8 RGBA16Sint output (the slice's class comes from that format) is poisoned with 0xAB and fully covered by the four 4x4 blocks.

name: clamp-the-clip-fade-to-a-dyadic-smoothstep
rationale: The clip-fade range is authored as start 1 and end -1, so the fragment position (0.5, 0.5) at the single pixel centre maps through (x - end) / (start - end) to the dyadic 0.75 and 0.25 that air.clamp.v4f16 passes through untouched, and the smoothstep t*t*(3 - 2t) lands on 0.84375 and 0.15625 exactly. The three air.fmin.f16 calls reduce to 0.15625, and the one-texel atlas holds the powers of two (1, 2, 4, 8), so the returned half4 is (0.15625, 0.3125, 0.625, 1.25) with no rounding anywhere. isHalo is zero so the faded arm is the one returned, and the case also pins that the fragment position is the pixel centre.

name: fragment-device-and-constant-pointer-integer-differences
rationale: One fragment invocation computes 12- and 28-byte interior-pointer differences through 64- and 32-bit integer conversions. No derived address is dereferenced. Input allocations are 32 and 48 bytes; stores cover bytes 8..40 of a 48-byte output and preserve both eight-byte canaries. Expected words: [0xcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcd,12,28,12,28,0xcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcd]. The vertex case disables rasterization; the fragment case uses a 1x1 attachmentless pass. Both source bodies are loop-free.

name: add-through-the-buffer-pair-a-runtime-switch-selects
rationale: The first authored case on a module that needs OpCapability VariablePointers. 49 corpus modules emit it and none had a case. MPSRNNAddSequenceData switches on threadgroup_position_in_grid.z and phis one of eight read_write device pointers against one of eight read-only ones, then adds through the selected pair -- a phi of pointers, which is exactly what the capability is for. The dispatch is 3 threads in z with one thread per threadgroup, so tgid.z is 0, 1 and 2 and three different arms of the switch run in one draw: the DEFAULT arm (z = 0, lhsBuffer1 += rhsBuffer1) and the first two labelled arms (z = 1 -> lhsBuffer2 += rhsBuffer2, z = 2 -> lhsBuffer3 += rhsBuffer3). x and y are 0 for every thread, so with wSize = (1, 1) the bounds guard passes and wRowStrideInElems * 0 + 0 selects element 0 of whichever buffer the phi chose. The observed binding is lhsBuffer2, the z = 1 arm, and every buffer is labelled so a wrong choice on either side is a different number: lhs k starts at 100 + k and rhs k holds k, so the answer is 102 + 2 = 104 and no other pairing gives it -- a phi that fell through to the default arm leaves 102, a phi that took the wrong rhs gives 102 + j, and a phi that wrote the wrong lhs leaves 102 here and corrupts a neighbour. Element 1 of the buffer is a -1 sentinel the kernel must not touch, so an off-by-one store is visible in the same eight observed bytes. Every value is a small integer exact in binary32, so the fast fadd has nothing to round.

name: layered-tracking-areas-scale-by-a-ceiled-depth
rationale: texture_layout = 2 with is_foveated off selects the layered branch, so the shader samples air.sample_depth_2d_array.f32 and air.sample_texture_2d_array.u.v4i16 at the slice its z coordinate names, and supports_shared_textures on selects the layered write, air.write_texture_2d_array.u.v4i16. The embedded sampler is nearest with pixel coordinates, so a per-view origin of (0.5,0.5) and (2.5,0.5) at unit size lands each thread exactly on one texel centre: slice 0 reads columns 0-1 and slice 1 reads columns 2-3, which is what makes the slice operand observable rather than incidental. Each result is ushort(value * ceil(depth)) with depths chosen so ceil is 0 for one texel per slice and 1 elsewhere, and every product (5, 0, 65535, 3, 300, 65535, 0, 40000) is exact in f32 and in range for the u16 truncation that stores it.

name: manual-float4-fetch-at-an-offset-transformed-onto-three-of-four-pixels
rationale: Reaching variant of this entry's manual-vertex-fetch case (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero constants gave a degenerate position. Constant 132 enables manual fetch; table slot 0 holds the same-library callback re::vertexfetch::fetchFromFloat4, and record 0 of the vertex-argument buffer (15 records of 24 bytes, the rest null) points at float4 positions with stride 16 and offset 16, which skips a leading decoy vertex (40, 40, 40). The three positions are (-1, -1), (3, -1), (-1, 3) with z = 1/4 with the matrix z scale 2, so world z = 5/8. The instance matrix (objectToCrWorld, column-major) scales x and y by 1/2, scales z and translates by (-1/4, -1/4, 1/8); crWorldToProjArray[0] keeps x, y and w and maps z to z/2 + 1/16, so the clip triangle is (-3/4, -3/4), (5/4, -3/4), (-3/4, 5/4) at w = 1. It covers the pixel centres (-1/2, 1/2), (-1/2, -1/2) and (1/2, -1/2) of the 2x2 target with a margin of at least 1/4 from every edge and misses (1/2, 1/2): pixel (1, 0) keeps its fill. The depth is the same at all three vertices, so its interpolation is exact; every product and sum is a small dyadic value, exact in float with or without contraction, and the observer writes (x + 1/2, y + 1/2, z, 1) for each covered pixel. screenSpaceDepthBias = 1/4 adds 1/4 * w to clip z: depth 0.625.

name: manual-vertex-fetch-null-buffer-defaults
no_effect: Zero instance and view constants give a degenerate position: the primitive covers no fragment, so the render target keeps its authored bytes.
rationale: Function constant 132 enables manual vertex fetch. Every zero-initialized embedded vertex-buffer pointer is null, so each AIR guard bypasses its table lookup and supplies the defined default attribute. Slot zero is the exact same-library invalid-format callback that supplies the table's required type but is unreachable. Optional video modes are disabled and zero transform constants produce a deterministic degenerate position. Buffer 30 and its reflected offset-zero device buffer are now authored explicitly; the invalid-format callback deterministically supplies the same default attribute when that first record is reached.

name: indexed-draw-reads-past-its-uint16-index-buffer-from-an-offset
rationale: Twelve 16-bit indices from byte 4 of an eight-index buffer: positions 6 to 11 read past it (DESIGN D258), and the two indices before the offset (0xFFFF) are never read. The oracle shadows 16 bytes past the buffer; the candidate's fetch is bounded by robustBufferAccess2 or clamped by the binder (D223).

name: indexed-draw-reads-past-its-uint32-index-buffer
rationale: Sixteen indices from a buffer of four (0 to 3): positions 4 to 15 read past it (DESIGN D258). Metal's API validation rejects such a draw and Metal states no result, so the oracle draws from the buffer with a 48-byte shadow (indices 0xE7E7E7E7) and records zero for seen[4..8]; the candidate's index fetch is bounded by robustBufferAccess2 (index 0) or clamped by the binder (D223).

name: fast-variant-reach-of-the-five-biggest-families
rationale: SPIRV-Cross emits the UNQUALIFIED MSL name for GLSL Exp, Pow, Log, InverseSqrt and Sqrt, and whether Metal resolves that to fast:: or precise:: is a property of MoltenVK's compile options rather than of anything this translator controls; it is already known to differ per function, since sqrt is approximate under MoltenVK's default and atan is not. This case settles it for the five biggest fast_ families in the corpus at once -- air.fast_powr (8320 call sites), air.fast_exp (7297), air.fast_rsqrt (6209), air.fast_pow (4904) and air.fast_log (2682), with air.fast_sqrt (7862) as the already-known control. Each argument was chosen to maximize the gap between the two variants over 20000 arguments per family on an Apple M3 Max, so no row is a coin flip: powr(19.193, 5.36) is 36 ULP apart, powr(16.572, 4.43) 34, exp(17.309) and exp(18.02) 15 each, log(1.0590001) 4, log(0.976) 3, sqrt 2 and rsqrt 1. Under xcrun metal defaults the unqualified spelling is bit-identical to fast:: on all 20000 arguments of every one of the five, so this fixture compiled normally emits air.fast_* and the Metal oracle is the fast column throughout: a Match says MoltenVK reaches fast:: as well, and a Mismatch would name exactly which families it does not. Every argument is read from a buffer so nothing folds, and each result is bit-cast into a uint so the comparison is exact. ANSWERED: Match on all ten rows, so MoltenVK reaches fast:: for exp, powr, log, rsqrt and sqrt and those five families -- 29274 corpus call sites -- are byte-exact with the single-opcode lowering they already have; the precise::-only set stays confined to the arctangent/tangent family.

name: a-tail-that-breaks-two-loops-records-which-lanes-run-it-together
rationale: The D44 multi-level-break exit tail with a tangled operation in it (control Q1, STATUS: the Q1 case must include this shape). One simdgroup of 32 threads. Lane t walks a nested do-while loop, outer i < trips[0] = 3, inner j < trips[1] = 4 (both authored inputs), and at its flat stop iteration i * 4 + j == stop[t] runs the tail: mask = simd_or(1 << lane), then leaves both loops by returning from the inlined helper; out[2t] = mask (0 if the lane never stops), out[2t + 1] = i << 8 | j at the stop, 0xFFFF otherwise. stop[t] = 7t mod 17: each flat stop 0..11 belongs to two lanes (t and t + 17, e.g. stop 0 to lanes 0 and 17, stop 4 = (1, 0) to lanes 3 and 20) except stops 3 and 10 (lanes 15 and 16 alone), so 22 lanes stop, spread over all three outer and all four inner iterations, and the 10 lanes with stops 12..16 never stop. The mask therefore reads which lanes execute the tail together: only the lanes stopping at the same (i, j) if AGX runs the tail in the inner iteration where each lane leaves (what D44's rule gives the compiled shape), the stopping lanes of one outer iteration if it runs after the inner loop, or all 22 if after both loops. The front end has no goto and compiles the break (as it does a flag-and-break spelling) with one join per loop: both inner exits meet in one block that re-tests the stop compare to leave the outer loop (D128). Bounded by the authored inputs: the inner loop runs at most max(trips[1], 1) = 4 times per outer iteration (its exit is `j + 1 == umax(trips[1], 1)`) and the outer loop at most trips[0] = 3 times (exit `i + 1 >= trips[0]`, unsigned), so each lane makes at most 12 inner and 3 outer header visits, far below the default fuel; no function constant is involved. Each lane writes only its own two words, which differ from the 0xAB poison.

name: compact-four-tile-occupancy-masks-into-one-location-run
rationale: Four tile-occupancy bitmasks are compacted into one contiguous run of tile locations, and every value in the answer is an integer the host fixes. Each of the 256 threads takes tile = gid >> 3 and sub = gid & 7, so the 16x16 grid is exactly four 8x8 tile groups and each group visits all 64 bit positions once. The group is selected as constants.tile_groups_per_row * tile.y + tile.x with tile_groups_per_row = 2, and that is the ONLY member this case reads out of the 192-byte packed tiled_constants_t: read it as anything but 2 and two tile groups collide on one mask, so the constant is load-bearing rather than incidental. A thread survives the branch exactly when its bit is set in layer_group_infos[idx].tile_occupied_mask, and then writes its ushort2 grid position at prefix_sums[idx].tile_offset - prefix_sums[0].tile_offset + popcount(mask & ~(-1 << bit)) -- the number of set bits strictly below its own, which is the air.popcount.i64 under test. The four masks have popcounts 32, 2, 16 and 36, deliberately distinct so a mask read from the wrong record cannot produce the right run length, and the four tile_offsets are their prefix sums biased by 1000 so the subtraction is exercised rather than trivially zero. The 86 surviving threads fill slots 0..85 one to one and the four slots behind them keep their 0xCC poison. No two threads share a slot, so the answer does not depend on execution order, and the kernel contains no loop.

name: argmax-two-rows-of-ten-signed-shorts-an-unsigned-accumulator-gets-wrong
rationale:
No authored case reached `llvm.smax.i16`, which 9 corpus sources use; this kernel is MLX's `arg_reduce_general<short, ArgMax, 4>` and the call IS its running maximum, so its answer decides both output words. The case runs two rows of ten with `ndim` 1, `shape` (2), `in_strides` (10), `out_strides` (1), `axis_stride` 1 and `axis_size` 10: two threadgroups of thirty-two threads, so threads 0..31 reduce row 0 -- where `gid < lsize` short-circuits `elem_to_loc` and both offsets are 0 -- and threads 32..63 reduce row 1, where both index loops actually run. Each thread reads four consecutive axis elements, so with an axis of ten only threads 0, 1 and 2 see real data and the other twenty-nine see nothing but the identity the out-of-range guard supplies.

Signedness is the case, and its counterfactual is stated exactly: the running accumulator is the only thing `llvm.smax.i16` decides -- the index test beside it and the comparison in the cross-lane reduction are `icmp` and stay signed whatever the call lowers to. Simulating this kernel with the accumulator replaced by an unsigned maximum and everything else unchanged answers indices 2 and 7 where the correct lowering answers 4 and 3. Both rows separate, and they separate differently: row 0 is 3, -1, 2, -2, 7, -3, 5, -9, -8, -6, mixed-sign small values whose maximum is 7 at index 4 while the unsigned maximum latches onto a negative early; row 1 is 7, -20000, 30000, 32000, 0, -1, 32000, 5, -3, 12, where the true answer is the first of two equal extrema. Row 1's repeat -- 32000 at indices 3 and 6 -- is also the tie rule: the per-thread scan advances its index only on a STRICT improvement and the simd reduction prefers the smaller index on an equal value, so 3 is the only correct answer and 6 is exactly what a non-strict comparison gives.

The extrema sit in different threads' four-element windows -- row 0's in thread 1, row 1's in thread 0 with a runner-up in thread 1 -- so the cross-lane `air.simd_shuffle_down.s.i16` pair reduction has to run for either row to come out right. The input buffer carries four elements past the two rows that the `axis_size` guard must never read. The output buffer is four words and only two are written; the other two must keep their 0x9C poison. `execution_safety` is `authored_bounded`: the AIR has six CFG cycles -- two `elem_to_loc` walks bounded by `ndim` = 1, the block loop bounded by ceil(axis_size / 4*lsize) = 1, two four-element inner loops, and the two shuffle reductions bounded by log2(simd_size) = 5.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-nine
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 9 and receives exact float4 zero from all eight linked _uber_clear bodies. An eleven-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; the final selector reads register 2 and writes exact zero to the poisoned primary texel.

name: blur-a-row-through-the-lane-above-and-wrap-the-last-lane
rationale:
A radius-1 separable Gaussian that never re-reads the texture for its side taps: each lane loads one texel at clamp_s(gid.x-1) and slides the window along the simdgroup with air.simd_shuffle_down.f32, so lane L's centre and +1 taps are lane L+1's and L+2's loaded value. Lane 31 has no lane above it, so it takes air.simd_shuffle_rotate_down.f32 of a second register that every lane pre-loaded at min_s(gid.x-1+32, W-1); the rotate wraps lane 0's copy down to lane 31, which is the texel one past lane 31's window. The threadgroup is a single 32-lane simdgroup and the grid is 32 wide, so every lane writes and the wrap path is taken on both rows. Row 0 puts a spike at x=31, so lane 31's answer is non-zero and can only come out right if the rotate landed -- 32*(w0+w1) = 27.724873.
air.abs.s.i16 is the weight-table index: the loop counter runs -1, 0, 1 and abs selects weights[1], weights[0], weights[1]. It is a loop-carried phi rather than a constant, so it is really evaluated three times per lane. air.clamp.s.i16 and air.min.s.i16 build the two load coordinates.
Exactness, and the reason for the spike layout: the arithmetic is fast-math, so the three-term sum may be reassociated, and an earlier draft with a fully populated row disagreed with Metal by one ulp in exactly the one output whose three taps were all non-zero. The spikes are therefore at least three apart, so no output ever sums three non-zero terms. The only multi-term outputs are at the two ends, where the clamp makes both live taps read the same texel: their sum is a power of two times (w0+w1) and scaling by a power of two commutes with rounding, so it is identical under every association. The generator asserts this directly -- it evaluates all six orderings under both a multiply-then-add and an FMA model and requires all twelve to produce one f32.
